# NetworkServicesGateway

`networkservices.gcp.hfl.dev/v1beta1`

**Gap it fills.** Terraform's `google_network_services_gateway`. A gateway: an OPEN_MESH gateway's listener, or a Secure Web Proxy (SECURE_WEB_GATEWAY) in a VPC network.

**Source.** generated by `hack/discokind` from the networkservices.v1 Discovery document.

## Notes

Generated by `hack/discokind` from `hack/discokind/kinds.yaml` (`docs/design.md`
section 2.4); its test is `pkg/discokind/kindtest` with the fixtures under
`pkg/controller/direct/networkservices/testdata/discokind/NetworkServicesGateway/`.

Why ours (2026-11-13): Config Connector's `networkservices.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1`
`NetworkServicesGateway` (at 1.160.0) has no `network`, `subnetwork`,
`gatewaySecurityPolicy`, `certificateUrls`, `labels` or `routingMode`, and
requires `scope`, so it cannot make a Secure Web Proxy. Ours keeps its
name (design.md decision 18) at `v1beta1` (decision 26) with the API's
whole field set, for both types. A workload moves to ours by acquiring the
same gateway.

The two types:

- `SECURE_WEB_GATEWAY` (a Secure Web Proxy): regional; `network`,
  `subnetwork`, `routingMode` and `gatewaySecurityPolicy` set, and the
  region needs an active proxy-only subnet (`REGIONAL_MANAGED_PROXY`) in
  the network. The fixtures are `create.yaml` and `update.yaml`; the live
  Setup (`gateway_test.go`) makes the network, both subnets and the
  policy.
- `OPEN_MESH`: global, with a `scope`; the fixtures are under
  `open-mesh/`, run by `TestNetworkServicesGatewayOpenMesh`
  (`kindtest.RunCase`).

Immutable fields (CEL): `type`, and those Terraform's
`google_network_services_gateway` forces a new gateway for: `addresses`,
`ports`, `scope`, `network`, `subnetwork`, `ipVersion`, `envoyHeaders`
and `routingMode`; `allPorts` and `allowGlobalAccess` are taken as
`ports` is. `description`, `labels`, `gatewaySecurityPolicy`,
`certificateUrls` and `serverTlsPolicy` are patched.

A Secure Web Proxy makes a Cloud Router with a Cloud NAT
(`swg-autogen-router-<n>`) in its network and region. The API keeps it
after the last gateway in that network and region is deleted, and the
network cannot be deleted while it is there. Ours does not delete it, as
Terraform does not unless `delete_swg_autogen_router_on_destroy` is set;
whoever deletes the network deletes the router first. The live test's
cleanup and the sweeper do.
